approach: For the block to stay on the frictionless incline, the string tension along the slope must balance gravity's pull along the slope, and this tension also supports the hanging mass.

steps.text: On the frictionless incline, the only forces on the small block along the slope are gravity's component down the slope and the string tension up the slope.
Compute this tension using m₁ = 1 kg, g = 10 m/s², sin30° = 0.5.
The same string, over the pulley, holds the hanging block M in place, so the tension also equals the hanging block's weight.

common_mistakes.text: Using cos30° instead of sin30° for the component of gravity along the incline gives M = m₁cos30° ≈ 0.87 kg.
Setting the tension equal to the full weight of the small block instead of its component along the incline gives M = m₁ = 1 kg.
